# shyft-hydrology

![Version: 0.0.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-0.0.2-informational?style=flat-square)  ![AppVersion: 37.3.0-1.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/AppVersion-37.3.0--1.1-informational?style=flat-square)

Shyft hydrology micro-services with a persistent core and scalable drms compute nodes.

Kubernetes: `>=1.30.0-0`

<!-- Generated by helm-docs from README.md.gotmpl and values.yaml. Edit those, then run `mise run docs`. -->

## What it deploys

| Workload | Kind | Runs | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core` | StatefulSet, always 1 pod | task, rmd, parameter, state, dtss, dstm, stm, goal_function: one container each | the databases, on one volume at `/shyft-var` |
| `drms` | Deployment, `drms.replicaCount` pods | one drms compute node per pod | none |

Also: one Service for the core services, two NetworkPolicies, a ServiceAccount, and optionally a
PodDisruptionBudget for drms. There is no Ingress: Shyft's protocol is binary and has no authentication.

The layout is upstream's
[podman pod](https://gitlab.com/shyft-os/shyft/-/wikis/How-to/Run-a-complete-Shyft-micro-service-system-with-podman):
the core services share a pod and find each other on `localhost`. Each drms registers its own pod IP with
task and re-registers every 5 seconds, so drms pods can come and go.

## Install

```sh
helm repo add shyft https://lazyoldbear.github.io/shyft-deployment
helm install shyft-hydrology shyft/shyft-hydrology --version 0.0.2 --namespace shyft --create-namespace
helm test shyft-hydrology --namespace shyft
```

The defaults fit a laptop. For real work start from a profile in [`examples/`](examples/):

| Profile | For |
|---|---|
| [`sigma2-nird.yaml`](examples/sigma2-nird.yaml) | Sigma2 NIRD: mirrored image, base port 22000, 8 drms of 16 CPU / 64 GiB, both existing claims |
| [`aws-eks.yaml`](examples/aws-eks.yaml) | AWS EKS: gp3 volume, drms node group, internal Network Load Balancer |
| [`azure-aks.yaml`](examples/azure-aks.yaml) | Azure AKS: managed disk, drms node pool, internal load balancer |

The profiles are validated against the Kubernetes API schemas in CI. They have not been run on NIRD, AWS or
Azure yet.

## Connect

Each service listens on `basePort + 2·n`:

| Service | n | Port at base 20000 | In the Service |
|---|---|---|---|
| task | 0 | 20000 | yes |
| rmd | 1 | 20002 | yes |
| parameter | 2 | 20004 | yes |
| state | 3 | 20006 | yes |
| drms | 4 | 20008 | no: task reaches each drms by pod IP |
| dtss | 5 | 20010 | yes |
| dstm | 6 | 20012 | yes |
| stm | 7 | 20014 | yes |
| goal_function | 8 | 20016 | yes |

**From a pod in the cluster.** Shyft's Python `HydroServiceConfig` reads two variables:

```sh
SHYFT_SERVICE_HOST=shyft-hydrology.shyft.svc
SHYFT_SERVICE_BASE_PORT=20000
```

With the default NetworkPolicy, pods in the release namespace may connect and others may not.

**From your machine.** `helm install` prints the `kubectl port-forward` command. Then use `localhost`.
One catch: a model run that asks the drms to store statistics passes it a dtss address
(`DrmsSaveStatisticsArgs.dtss_host_port`). The drms resolves that address itself, so give it the Service
name (`shyft-hydrology:20010`), not `localhost`.

**From your network.** Set `service.type: LoadBalancer`, `service.cloud` to your cloud (`aws`, `azure` or
`gke`) and that cloud's internal load balancer annotation, as in the profiles, and add your client network to
`networkPolicy.clientPeers`. The chart refuses to render a load balancer without the named cloud's annotation,
or with any annotation that asks for a public one. It cannot see which cloud it really runs on: an annotation
meant for another cloud is ignored there, and the load balancer comes out public. The install notes print the
command that shows the address; check that it is private.

## Storage

- `persistence.var` holds every database, under `/shyft-var/<service>/db`. By default the chart creates one
  claim through the StatefulSet. `helm uninstall` keeps it, and a later install with the same release name
  and namespace finds the data again.
- Set `persistence.var.existingClaim` to use a claim you already have.
- The size and storage class of the created claim cannot be changed through the chart afterwards: Kubernetes
  does not allow it on a StatefulSet. Resize the claim itself if your storage class supports it.
- `persistence.data` mounts an existing claim with input data at `/shyft-data`, in the core containers and,
  with `mountInDrms`, in the drms pods.
- Leave headroom: RocksDB preallocates its log files, so even empty databases take a few hundred MiB.

## Scaling drms

Change `drms.replicaCount`. A new drms registers with task within seconds. A drms that is stopped
normally unregisters first.

Task never expires a registration. A drms that dies without a chance to unregister (out of memory, a lost
node, a spot instance reclaimed) stays in task's queue. Each time task picks it, the run waits about 2
seconds and moves on to the next one. Restarting the core pod clears the queue; the live drms pods register
again within 5 seconds. So:

- Do not run drms on spot or preemptible nodes.
- A run that is on a drms when it dies fails. Task does not retry it; submit it again.

## Security

- No authentication in the protocol: whoever reaches a port can read and write. Keep the Service internal.
- NetworkPolicies are on by default. They only work if the cluster's network plugin enforces them. With a
  load balancer they are the second barrier: only the networks in `networkPolicy.clientPeers` get through.
- Containers run as uid and gid 1000 (user `ci` in the image), with a read-only root filesystem, no
  capabilities, no privilege escalation and no service account token. Every pod, the test pods included,
  is admitted in a namespace that enforces the `restricted` Pod Security Standard.

## Tests

`helm test` runs a read-only check: every core service must answer through the Service.

The test pods run the Shyft image. It is amd64 only, so on a cluster with arm64 nodes give the workloads and
the tests a node selector (`core.nodeSelector`, `drms.nodeSelector`, `tests.nodeSelector`), and tolerations
if your nodes are tainted.

With `tests.modelRun.enabled: true` it also seeds Shyft's demo model and runs it: task picks a drms, the drms
computes and stores statistics in dtss, and the test reads the results back. That test writes demo data into
the databases. Use it on a fresh install or in CI, not on a system with real data.

## Upgrades

The chart version is the chart's own SemVer: 0.0.2 deploys Shyft
37.3.0-1.1 (`appVersion`). While it is 0.x, a minor version may change values in ways
that need your attention: the changelog says how. A chart upgrade restarts
the core pod and keeps the data. Moving to another Shyft major may need a database migration that this chart
does not do: read the Shyft release notes first.

### 06. Storage

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| persistence.var.enabled | bool | `true` | Keep the service databases on a PersistentVolume. `false` uses an emptyDir: data is lost with the pod. |
| persistence.var.existingClaim | string | `""` | Use this existing claim instead of creating one. It must allow writes from the core pod's user. |
| persistence.var.storageClass | string | `""` | Storage class of the created claim. Empty uses the cluster default. |
| persistence.var.accessModes | list | `["ReadWriteOnce"]` | Access modes of the created claim. |
| persistence.var.size | string | `"10Gi"` | Size of the created claim. It cannot be changed through the chart later. |
| persistence.data.enabled | bool | `false` | Mount an existing claim with input data into the core containers. |
| persistence.data.existingClaim | string | `""` | The claim to mount. Required when enabled; the chart never creates it. |
| persistence.data.mountPath | string | `"/shyft-data"` | Where to mount it. |
| persistence.data.readOnly | bool | `false` | Mount it read-only. |
| persistence.data.mountInDrms | bool | `false` | Also mount it into drms pods. With more than one node this needs a ReadWriteMany (or ReadOnlyMany) claim. |

### 07. Network

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| service.type | string | `"ClusterIP"` | Service type for the core services. `LoadBalancer` is rendered only with an annotation that makes it internal: Shyft's protocol has no authentication. |
| service.cloud | string | `""` | With `type: LoadBalancer`: the cloud the cluster runs in. The chart then requires that cloud's internal load balancer annotation in `annotations`: another cloud's annotation does nothing there, and the load balancer would be public. |
| service.annotations | object | `{}` | Service annotations, for example the cloud's internal load balancer annotation. |
| networkPolicy.enabled | bool | `true` | Create NetworkPolicies: core accepts drms, the chart's test pods and the clients below; drms accepts only core. They need a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy. |
| networkPolicy.allowNamespace | bool | `true` | Let every pod in the release namespace connect to the core services. |
| networkPolicy.clientPeers | list | `[]` | Who else may connect to the core services, as NetworkPolicy peers: a `podSelector`, a `namespaceSelector`, or with a load balancer an `ipBlock` for your client network. |

### 08. Security

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| serviceAccount.create | bool | `true` | Create a ServiceAccount. The pods never talk to the Kubernetes API and mount no token. |
| serviceAccount.name | string | `""` | Name of the ServiceAccount. Empty uses the release's full name, or `default` when `create` is false. |
| serviceAccount.annotations | object | `{}` | ServiceAccount annotations. |
| podSecurityContext | object | `{"fsGroup":1000,"fsGroupChangePolicy":"OnRootMismatch","runAsGroup":1000,"runAsNonRoot":true,"runAsUser":1000,"seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"}}` | Pod security context of every pod. uid and gid 1000 are user `ci` in the Shyft image. On storage that ignores `fsGroup` (NFS), set the uid and gid that own the directory. |
| securityContext | object | `{"allowPrivilegeEscalation":false,"capabilities":{"drop":["ALL"]},"readOnlyRootFilesystem":true}` | Container security context of every container. The root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is an emptyDir. |
